name: DBMS-20
tagline: DEC's CODASYL network database for the 36-bit DECsystem-10 and DECSYSTEM-20 mainframes.
description: DBMS-20 was Digital Equipment Corporation's CODASYL (DBTG-style) network database for the DECSYSTEM-20 running TOPS-20, the sibling of DBMS-10 on the DECsystem-10, whose first manuals date from September 1973. Data was described with a schema DDL of areas, record types and owner-member sets, applications received tailored sub-schemas, and COBOL programs navigated records through an embedded data-manipulation language handled by a run-time Data Base Control System. The last documented release, V6.1, appears in DEC's 1985 TOPS-20 documentation set. It died with DEC's 36-bit product line and is now a reference point for how navigational databases worked before SQL took over.
statusNote: Shipped by DEC from the 1970s to the mid-1980s (last documented release V6.1, c. 1985); ended with the 36-bit DECsystem line.

pricing.notes: Was licensed per computer system by DEC; no longer sold.

strengths: Faithful implementation of the CODASYL DBTG schema/sub-schema and set model
Complete DEC manuals survive on bitsavers, making it a well-documented teaching example
Sub-schemas gave each program a restricted view of the database, an early form of access control
weaknesses: Runs only on long-obsolete DEC 36-bit hardware or emulators
Navigational record-at-a-time access couples programs tightly to physical structure
useCases: Understanding the pre-relational design that SQL replaced
